# EVAL.md — detector evaluation (WS-C)

*Generated by `just eval` (`ml/scripts/eval.jl`) on 2026-09-09 08:24:06 UTC. Do not edit by hand.*

## What was measured

5 seeds x 120 held-out virtual nodes x 150 s, simulated by `ml/src/sim.jl`
(the Julia reimplementation of the WS-B twin dynamics), with gamma-renewal
parameters drawn from `ml\artifacts\twin_params.json`.

Both detectors are calibrated to the **same false-alarm rate** (target α = 1.0 %) on a
separate calibration cohort before evaluation, so lead time is compared at a matched
operating point rather than bought with extra false positives.

Calibrated thresholds: z-score `stress >= 0.9767`, GRU `stress >= 0.9474`.

Both detectors are run **online**, one 1 s feature window at a time, exactly
as `services/feature-worker` runs them: each learns its own per-node baseline
from the first 30 windows and may only declare a state after 2 consecutive
alarm windows. Neither sees a label. Windows inside the warm-up are excluded
from the scores, since both detectors are required to stay silent there.

- **z-score**: unsupervised diagonal Hotelling *T²* drift on the 8-feature
  vector, with a rule-based class assignment. No training.
- **GRU**: Flux `GRU(8 => 32)` over 30-window sequences, 4-class softmax,
  stress = 1 − P(baseline). Trained by `just train` (seed 42, 300 nodes,
  val accuracy 0.578).

## Headline: lead time

**Lead time** = `symptom_onset − first sustained alarm`, in seconds.
`symptom_onset` is the WIRE §6 ground-truth event (a node's firing rate below
5 % of its own baseline for ≥ 2 s). Positive means the detector warned
*before* the node visibly collapsed. Mean ± std across seeds.

| detector | lead time (s) | collapsing nodes detected | ROC-AUC | false-alarm rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| z-score | 8.18 ± 3.78 | 35.8 ± 7.7 % | 0.674 ± 0.017 | 0.03 ± 0.03 % |
| GRU | 12.41 ± 1.84 | 64.3 ± 8.2 % | 0.723 ± 0.009 | 0.03 ± 0.03 % |

The GRU warns **4.23 s earlier** than the z-score baseline on average.

Per-node lead-time distribution (GRU, all seeds pooled, n = 110): median 10.0 s, 10th pct 0.0 s, 90th pct 30.2 s.

## What this is not

Lead time is measured in **seconds** against a *simulated* collapse
endpoint (firing rate below 5 % of the node's own baseline), not days of
clinical prodrome. The GRU is trained on labels from `ml/src/sim.jl` (the
twin generator), not on in-vivo pharmacology. It is a 4-class sequence
classifier (`GRU(8 => 32)`). A tiny Transformer encoder (`d_model=32`, 4 heads,
2 layers) is trained by `just train --arch transformer` on the **same** 8×30
twin sequences; it is not a day-scale clinical model and does not ingest
RNA-seq. See `docs/METHODS.md` and `docs/FUTURE.md`.

Online `feature-worker` prefers `DETECTOR=transformer` then GRU then z-score.
`/metrics` exports `feature_worker_transformer_loaded` and
`feature_worker_gru_loaded`. The numbers in the tables above are GRU vs
z-score; re-run `just eval` after training the Transformer to add that row.

## How to reproduce

```sh
just prepare   # fit twin_params.json from data/raw (or synthetic fallback)
just train     # ml/artifacts/gru.bson
just train --arch transformer
just eval      # regenerates this file
```

Every number above comes from a seeded, re-runnable script; no result is
hand-entered. See `docs/METHODS.md` for data provenance and what is real vs
synthetic.
